blocks.content: Ethan walked with no firm destination, which was how he usually found the best places. Planning too hard made his art stiff. Wandering gave it room to breathe.

He paused at the narrow alley painted with a faded mural from some festival years ago. Good composition. The ivy splitting the bricks in uneven lines. The peeling color still confident despite itself.
Then laughter carried from down the street.
He knew before he looked.
That was ridiculous. He had heard her laugh once. He had no business recognizing it.
But he did.
Cassandra crossed toward the park with her friend, still carrying the purple dinosaur. She moved through the town like she was collecting pieces of it.
Don't stare.
He stared anyway. Because something about her seemed impossible to sketch quickly enough.
Then, as if the world wanted to punish him for noticing, she turned.
For half a second, their eyes met.
Ethan froze. She didn't.
She smiled. Not a big smile. Not a romantic one. Just a quick, bright flash of acknowledgement sent across the street like a thrown match.
It lit something anyway.
Ethan looked down immediately, pretending to search his bag.
Smooth. Very normal. Award-winning human behavior.
When he looked up, she was walking away. But the smile stayed behind. Annoyingly.

Cassandra had noticed him. The sketchbook guy from the café window — standing near the alley with a bag over one shoulder and a coffee in hand, looking like he had been caught doing something illegal by accident.
Oddly endearing.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: Who are you smiling at?

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: No one.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: That was not a no-one smile.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: There are categories now?

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: Absolutely. That was at least a someone-adjacent smile.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: He was just standing there.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: Men do be standing.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Lena.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: I'm observing.
Cassandra glanced back once more, but the guy had started walking the opposite direction, head down, shoulders slightly hunched like he was apologizing to the sidewalk for taking up space.
Not pity. Recognition. Some people hid behind volume. Some behind silence. She knew a thing or two about hiding in plain sight.
